impact: The before/after split handle (`#split-handle`) uses `role="slider"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"` — but the handle moves left/right, its aria-valuenow is a horizontal percentage, and horizontal is the actual slider axis. Vertical is for handles that move up/down; screen readers will read this as up/down and users won't know which arrow keys apply. Also, `.split-handle:focus-visible { outline: none; }` removes the keyboard focus indicator entirely; the only visual is a subtle grip transform, which is a fragile substitute. Set aria-orientation to horizontal (or drop it — horizontal is the default) and restore a visible focus outline on the handle.
resolution: index.html: aria-orientation changed from "vertical" to "horizontal" on #split-handle — matches ArrowLeft/ArrowRight keyboard handler in src/main.js:336-340. src/style.css: replaced `.split-handle:focus-visible { outline: none }` with a visible 2.5px accent outline on the grip with 3px offset, keeping the existing scale/shadow affordance for hover. Build validation blocked by pre-existing ISS-009 (vite/svgo mismatch); changes are HTML/CSS-only and independently verifiable.
title: Split handle: wrong aria-orientation and outline:none breaks a11y
